videos.script: A shop's inbox fills up every morning. Most messages are about parcels, refunds, payments and passwords. A few are about nothing the shop does. {{inbox}} A prize draw. A job application. A question about lasagne. Somebody has to find those before they waste anyone's time. {{odd}} You cannot train a model on them, because they have nothing in common. Next week's will be different again. {{nothing}} So this lesson turns the question around. It describes what normal looks like, and measures how far each new message is from it. {{region}} You will try two ways to measure that distance. One misses a piece of spam. The other finds all eight odd messages. {{scores}} Then you will choose where to draw the line, using normal messages the detector has never seen. {{threshold}} In the second week the shop launches a subscription, and normal moves. You will see that happen in a whole batch at once. {{drift}} And you will see what a detector like this cannot catch: a message that is dangerous and perfectly on topic. {{end}}
